verdicts.note: Mentions a side-detection message but explicitly states 'the main issue is the transmission'.
Oil leak and engine gasket, not coolant -- ENGINE is right and the two ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING answers are model errors.
'Center U joint' is a driveshaft component, so POWER TRAIN (driveline) is correct.
Stated main concerns are paint and air conditioning, neither of which any class covers; UNKNOWN OR OTHER holds.
Wobble occurs specifically when shifting between 1st and 2nd gear, tying it to the drivetrain rather than suspension.
Fire correctly routed to its causal system (transmission tubes) per the fire-handling rule.
Brake pull with no hydraulic/air/electric detail -- same overlapping-definition problem as 840438.
Fatal crash where the seat belt came loose AND the airbag failed to deploy. Two distinct failures, both named; either label is defensible.
Two separate complaints: loss of acceleration/near-stall and steering lockup on left turns. Multi-issue.
BORDERLINE: 'jerks then picks up more speed' reads like speed control, but the stuck shifter anchors it to the drivetrain.
Genuinely multi-issue (transmission, engine-bay fire, wheels loosening), but all models chose POWER TRAIN anyway so widening would not change any score.
Diagnosed bad throttle body; the VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL definition explicitly covers throttle/accelerator-pedal faults.

Airbag light plus wipers, cabin lights and radio all misbehaving, with the complainant checking fuses and wiring and concluding 'cause of problems unknown'. A general electrical read is as defensible as the airbag one.

All three models said ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING. Head-gasket failure is an engine internal but is precisely a coolant-sealing failure, and the narrative never explicitly names overheating or coolant, so neither reading can be called wrong.
Outer tie rod replaced repeatedly. Same STEERING/SUSPENSION boundary the earlier adjudication accepted as ambiguous for the 'death wobble' row (1278059).
